transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

The E:15 code on your Bosch SMV4HTX31E means the anti-flood system has detected water in the base pan, which is why the pump keeps running to prevent flooding. This usually happens because of a leak (from the door seal, spray arms, or hoses) rather than a faulty switch itself. To find the source, please check if the rubber door seal looks damaged or if anything was caught in it, and inspect the inlet and drain hose connections at the back for any drips.
Door seal looks okay. The unit's fully integrated under the worktop so I can't pull it out to get at the hoses. I can see a little shine of water in the base tray through a gap by the plinth though.

The E:15 code suggests water has reached the base pan. Since the door seal looks fine and you can't access the rear hoses easily, the leak is likely coming from inside the machine (such as a loose sump hose or pump seal) rather than an external connection. To confirm this, please switch off the mains power and remove the plinth at the bottom front to inspect the base pan directly. Look for a small white plastic box or float; if you see water in there or hoses dripping into it, that identifies the source as internal.
I can't remove the plinth, it's a continuous kitchen one glued at the ends and I'd damage it. Is there anything else I can check without taking it off?

Since you cannot access the base pan to drain it, we need to rule out a simple blockage that might be causing back-pressure or foam, which can sometimes trick the sensor. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher, then open the door and remove the lower rack. Twist and lift out the cylindrical filter at the bottom of the tub. Check if it is blocked with food or debris, and look into the sump (the hole underneath) to see if there is any standing water or foam there. This helps distinguish between a blockage issue and an active internal leak.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Filter was already fairly clean when I looked. Can't tell you about the sump, not sure what I'm meant to see in there. No foam, I only use tablets. What next?

Since the filter is clean and the door seal looks fine, but water is most likely sitting in the base pan (causing the E:15 code), the leak is probably internal—likely from the pump seals or an internal hose. As you can't access the plinth to drain this tray, we need to rule out a simple external blockage that might be causing pressure issues. Please check under the sink where the grey drain hose connects to your waste pipe; look for any drips there or if the hose is kinked. If that area is dry and the hose is clear, it suggests an internal leak that will require an engineer to access the base pan safely.
I'm not sure I can tell what's going on at the drain hose connection, I haven't looked there. There's no water on the kitchen floor at all. If it is an internal leak, is an engineer the only option?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, an engineer is the only option in this situation. The E:15 code suggests water has reached the base pan, and since you cannot remove the plinth to drain it, the machine will remain locked out until that water is removed. Because the door seal and filter are fine, the leak is likely internal (such as a pump seal or hose), which requires dismantling the appliance to fix. Please call an engineer; they can safely access the base pan, clear the fault, and repair the source of the leak.
